imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer standing on the green, watching as his golf ball is wedged between the flagstick and the rim of the hole, with part of the ball visible below the cup's edge.
imageAlt: Golf ball wedged on the flagstick at the hole with a teenage golfer watching.

issues: The ball is realistically wedged between the flagstick and hole with part below the lip, but slight additional cup detail could emphasize below-the-rim position even further.
Boy stands naturally, left-handed with a realistic putter and accurate kit—purple top, navy shorts, and cap.
One single believable golf ball and club. Proportions and posture are excellent.
Setting is a believable putting green in bright daylight.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Further emphasize part of the ball visible below the cup's rim by adding more visible cup edge height or perspective detail, making it clear the ball dips beneath the level of the putting surface.

questions.title: Ball stuck between the flag and the hole
questions.question: You hit a putt and your ball gets stuck between the flagstick and the edge of the hole, with part of your ball below the top of the hole. What happens?

choices.text: You have to play the ball from where it is
You need to take out the flag and hit the putt again
Your ball counts as in the hole
You get a penalty and have to take out the ball

questions.explanation: If your ball is stuck between the flagstick and the hole with some of it under the top edge, it counts as being in the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The stick that stands in the hole on the green so you can see where the hole is.
This means your ball has gone in the hole, so you have finished that shot.
The very top edge of the hole.

questions.teachingTip: Show what it looks like when the ball gets wedged between the flag and hole. Let children see how much of the ball must be under the lip for it to count.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think you have to replay the putt.
Some may think the ball is not in the hole if it is not at the very bottom.

questions.title: Ball wedged against the flagstick
questions.question: Your putt finishes with the ball wedged between the flagstick and the edge of the hole, with some of the ball below the lip. What is the ruling?

choices.text: You must play the ball from where it stopped
You must remove the flagstick and replay the shot
You get a penalty and remove the ball

questions.explanation: If your ball comes to rest wedged between the flagstick and the hole with part of it below the level of the lip, it's considered holed.
